Thank you all for your thorough reviews. Let me summarize what we have and what's outstanding before I can record final terms.

From Jonas (risk): The covenant testing file shows Harbor Point's leverage is 0.3x above the permitted level. Under workout policy, this means a covenant waiver is only allowed with a 9-month extension — not the 12 months requested — and requires a monthly leverage certificate throughout the extension period. Jonas still needs to attach the covenant testing file to the committee package.

From Mei (relationship): Harbor Point's owners have signed a term sheet committing to inject $1,200,000 of new equity at restructuring closing. Mei still needs to enter this signed term sheet in the relationship system.

From Rafael (legal): The senior lender must give written consent before any equipment collateral can be released, and that consent has not yet been requested. The $900,000 equipment release cannot proceed until this is obtained.

From Nadia (collateral): Receivables are the weakest and most volatile part of the collateral package, so under collateral policy a weekly borrowing-base certificate will be required throughout any extension period. Nadia still needs to update the monitoring schedule to reflect this.

Based on these findings, the restructuring cannot be finalized today. There are four outstanding items that must be completed first: (1) Jonas attaching the covenant testing file, (2) Mei entering the signed term sheet in the relationship system, (3) Rafael obtaining senior lender written consent for the equipment release, and (4) Nadia updating the monitoring schedule. Once these are resolved, I will record the final terms reflecting a 9-month extension, $1,200,000 equity injection, monthly leverage certificates, weekly borrowing-base certificates, and no equipment collateral release until senior lender consent is obtained.
